records: Checker predictions are based on average signal strength across an area.
Coverage can vary within a grid section because of local factors.
Ofcom combines operator predictions under a single independent standard.
The checker excludes 2G and 3G because those networks are being gradually switched off.
All four main network operators allow calls and texts over Wi-Fi.
Ofcom identifies legal repeaters as one possible way to improve indoor coverage.
The checker displays N/A or -1 for postal-district coverage when prediction data is unavailable.
Coverage and performance use different reporting methodologies.
Coverage scores are based on mobile-network-operator predictions.
Performance scores are based on crowdsourced measurements.
Mobile performance measurements are collected from smartphones every day under normal-use conditions.
Performance measurements include both indoor and outdoor locations.
Performance measurements are grouped into postal districts.
Ofcom says crowdsourced performance scores should be treated as a guide because local variation remains possible.
A mobile coverage complaint can be taken to an ADR scheme after eight unresolved weeks or earlier after a deadlock letter.
Ofcom's codes-of-practice page was published on 28 April 2010.
The codes-of-practice page was last updated on 16 July 2025.
The updated broadband speeds codes apply to purchases from 21 December 2022.
Section 52 of the Communications Act 2003 requires Ofcom to set general conditions for complaint handling and dispute resolution procedures.
General Condition C4 is the relevant condition for complaints handling and dispute resolution.
General Condition C4.2 requires providers to comply with procedures conforming to the Ofcom Approved Complaints Code.
General Condition C4.3 requires providers to belong to and comply with an approved ADR scheme.
A formal General Condition C4 non-compliance penalty can reach up to ten per cent of turnover under section 96.
The voluntary automatic compensation code took effect on 1 April 2019.
The automatic compensation code covers delayed repairs, missed engineer appointments and delayed starts of new services.
BT is listed as an automatic compensation scheme signatory.
EE is listed as an automatic compensation scheme signatory.
Hyperoptic is listed as an automatic compensation scheme signatory.
Plusnet, including John Lewis Broadband, is listed as an automatic compensation scheme signatory.
Sky, including NOW Broadband, is listed as an automatic compensation scheme signatory.
